sources.section: Document Management - Institutional Repository and Digital Library Software
sources.entry: Samvera Hyrax - Front-end for the Samvera framework, which itself is a Ruby on Rails application for browsing and managing Fedora-based digital repositories. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Ruby

summary.one_liner: Hyrax is a Ruby on Rails engine from the Samvera community that provides a foundation for building digital repository applications.
summary.what_it_does: Hyrax is a Rails Engine, not a standalone web app: you mount it inside a Rails application to build a Hyrax-based digital repository. It lets you create repository object types on demand and deposit content through multiple configurable workflows. Content can be described with flexible metadata. An administrative dashboard enables or disables optional features. The README also points to Docker-based local setup, documentation on the Samvera wiki, and a Helm chart for Kubernetes-style deployment.
use_cases: manage digital collections with custom metadata
configure deposit workflows for submitted content
how_to_run: Run Hyrax locally using Docker (see the Docker instructions in the README)
Develop your own Hyrax-based application by mounting the Hyrax engine in a Rails app
Follow the Hyrax Management Guide for production considerations
Use the Helm chart to deploy a Hyrax-based application to Kubernetes
stack: Fedora repository (implied by the Samvera/Fedora context)
notable: Rails Engine designed to be mounted inside a host Rails application rather than run alone
Create repository object types on demand
Admin dashboard for enabling or disabling optional features
Helm chart available for cloud Kubernetes deployments
Developed and maintained by the Samvera community
caveats: Not a web application on its own; a Hyrax-based Rails application must be built that mounts the engine
README does not describe the setup steps in detail; it links to external guides and the wiki
